correctness.rationale: The alternating vector is the unique eigenvector of the even-cycle Laplacian at eigenvalue 4; the exact scalar invariant map is x->x-4h sin x. H(a)=a/(2 sin a) increases bijectively from 1/2 to infinity. Both cycle points have the same derivative I-h cos(a)L on the mean-zero quotient, proving every Floquet factor and the stability boundary at pi/4. The convex endpoint spectral minimax gives the unique optimizer and closed finite-size rate. Lyapunov–Schmidt/implicit-function reduction is valid because at h=1/2 the only nontrivial -1 eigenspace is the alternating line, while every complementary squared eigenvalue differs from 1; the scalar two-return expansion gives a unique nearby squared amplitude y=12(h-1/2)+O((h-1/2)^2). Taylor expansions yield the n^-2 optimal step and gap. The embedded reproducible checker verifies finite return and spectral identities but not the universal claims; those follow from the displayed proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 ring source terminates its almost-global convergence analysis exactly at the loss of stability of the physically distinguished phase-opposition state and leaves larger-strength bifurcations untreated. The new theorem identifies what coherent periodic attractor actually emerges, establishes sharp persistence in all transverse Fourier modes despite possible additional instabilities of the parent fixed point, and gives an exact finite-size optimal interaction step and n^-2 damping gap. This is a natural, structural, parameter-wide solution to the first supercritical regime rather than an arbitrary sample or merely a renamed generic flip normal form. It makes no inflated global-basin claim.
